skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Browser automation skill for AI agents using inference.sh and Playwright. It can open pages, inspect element references, interact with forms, take screenshots, record video, use proxies, upload files, and run page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Automate browser sessions, page interactions, screenshots, and evidence capture through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-shell

security_audit.summary: The skill provides legitimate browser automation, but it also exposes high-risk capabilities: screenshots and video, proxy routing, arbitrary page JavaScript, and cookie extraction guidance. Most Markdown backtick, relative link, placeholder URL, and /dev/null matches are false positives. The remaining confirmed issues require strong authorization, data handling, and anti-abuse safeguards before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Cookie extraction guidance can expose authenticated session tokens.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples, or limit them to owned test systems with explicit authorization and redaction requirements.

remediation.issue: Proxy documentation includes rate limit avoidance and anonymity workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Replace evasion-oriented language with compliant geo-testing and corporate proxy examples, and require target authorization.

remediation.issue: The execute function can run arbitrary JavaScript in visited pages.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear constraints that JavaScript execution is only for authorized pages and must not collect secrets or private account data.

remediation.issue: Screenshots and video recordings can capture sensitive browser content.
remediation.suggestion: Keep recording disabled by default, warn users before capture, and document secure retention and deletion practices.

remediation.issue: Shell templates invoke external browser automation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add input validation for URLs and output paths, quote shell variables consistently, and tell users to inspect templates before running them.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows slow down research, testing, and evidence capture. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable browser automation workflow through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Open browser sessions and navigate to target URLs through inference.sh.
Return compact element references for clicking, filling, selecting, dragging, and uploading files.
Capture viewport or full page screenshots from active browser sessions.
Record browser sessions as video and return the recording when the session closes.
Run page JavaScript for content extraction and page inspection.
Route browser sessions through HTTP, HTTPS, or SOCKS proxy settings.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a working authenticated infsh setup.
Element references can become stale after navigation or dynamic page changes.
Screenshots and videos may capture sensitive content from visited pages.
Proxy, upload, and JavaScript execution features require careful authorization.

use_cases.title: Capture Test Evidence
use_cases.description: Record screenshots and videos that show a browser workflow before and after a release.

use_cases.title: Collect Web Research
use_cases.description: Open pages, inspect visible elements, extract page text, and save screenshots for review.

use_cases.title: Automate Repeated Forms
use_cases.description: Discover form element references, fill fields, submit pages, and verify success states.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the target page with agent-browser, summarize the page title, visible interactive elements, and next safe actions.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Known Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the latest snapshot refs to fill the form fields I provide, submit the form, and verify the result.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Workflow Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Run this browser workflow with screenshots at each key state and record video only when no sensitive data is shown.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Authorized Page Data
prompt_templates.prompt: For this authorized site, use snapshots and page JavaScript to extract visible text, links, and screenshots into reviewable outputs.

output_examples.input: Inspect a login page and identify the fields needed for automation.
output: The browser session opened the login page successfully.
The snapshot found email, password, remember me, and sign in controls.
A fresh snapshot is required after submitting the form.

output_examples.input: Capture evidence for a settings change workflow.
output: The workflow produced before and after screenshots.
The final page title and visible confirmation text were recorded.
Video recording was skipped because the session included account settings.

output_examples.input: Extract visible content from an authorized documentation page.
output: The page title, main headings, visible links, and full page screenshot were collected.
The results are ready for review without exposing credentials.

best_practices: Use the latest snapshot after every navigation, form submission, or dynamic page change.
Run automation only on sites and accounts where you have clear authorization.
Disable video recording and screenshots when pages may contain secrets or personal data.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse stale element references after a page change.
Do not use proxies to bypass access controls, rate limits, or site policies.
Do not extract cookies, tokens, or private account data from third-party sessions.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video recording, file upload, proxy use, and page JavaScript execution.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require an external service?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated infsh environment.

faq.question: Can it work with authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but users must avoid recording or exposing credentials, cookies, tokens, or private account data.

faq.question: Why do element references change?
faq.answer: References are tied to the current page snapshot and can change after navigation, form submission, or dynamic updates.

faq.question: What security review is needed before use?
faq.answer: Review proxy use, screenshots, video capture, JavaScript execution, and cookie handling against your authorization and data policies.
